images.title: Count the same 15 circles two ways
images.purpose: Shows Step 3 of the growing pattern counted two ways, as a 4 by 4 square with one missing and as a 3 by 3 square with two strips of 3, both giving 15 = k² + 2k.
images.composition: A before and after style comparison: the same circle arrangement twice, side by side, each grouped differently. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Each panel shows the same 15 circles: a 4 by 4 grid of circle positions with the bottom right position empty. Left panel: all 15 circles teal (#0072B2), a thin grey (#6B7280) square outline around the full 4 by 4 grid, and the empty bottom right position drawn as a dashed circle; label '4 × 4 − 1 = 15' below. Right panel: the top left 3 by 3 block of 9 circles teal, the 3 circles in the right column (top 3 rows) amber (#E69F00), and the 3 circles in the bottom row (left 3 columns) amber; label '3 × 3 + 3 + 3 = 15' below. Centred beneath both panels, the label 'both k² + 2k'. Exactly 15 circles in each panel.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Different ways of counting one pattern give the same expression.
images.description: Shows Step 3 of the growing pattern counted two ways, as a 4 by 4 square with one missing and as a 3 by 3 square with two strips of 3, both giving 15 = k² + 2k.
images.context: Step k: (k + 1)² − 1 = k² + 2k; Step 3 has 15, Step 10 has 120, Step 15 has 255.

image_decisions.why: The concept is that different groupings agree; two groupings of one arrangement show that directly.
